doc.title: Dave Rivello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012

title: Teaching at Eastman as 'super part time'
summary: He teaches, covers sabbaticals for colleagues, leads the New Jazz Ensemble and teaches jazz pedagogy.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: What’s it like working in academe?

I like it. I’m very committed to it and I take it as a big responsibility for the students’ futures. And it’s tiring in a way because I am committed to it, and I follow-up with these students that have been my students and find out how they’re doing if they’re in New York and what’s going on, and I try to stay in touch with them so that they know it wasn’t just the time that they were here, and then okay on to the next guy. You know I take it very seriously and I enjoy teaching, because the students also inspire me.
You’re not a full time — are you full time there?
No I’m — I call it “super part time.”
But right now, the last few years I’ve been “sabbatical replacement guy,” that’s also my invented title for myself. But Clay Jenkins was on sabbatical a couple of years ago so I

covered his classes. And then last fall Bill Dobbins was on sabbatical so I taught all the jazz writing courses and his private students. This year Harold Danko was on sabbatical in the fall so I covered that, and then Dariusz Terefenko is on sabbatical this coming semester so I’m covering his thing. So it’s been very busy. But then after this year they’ve all had sabbaticals so then I’m back to “super part time” thing.
Super part time guy. There’s some advantage to that, isn’t there?

Yes. And I mean I love leading a band, and so the New Jazz Ensemble is just always a blast, and I program the music that I believe in, and the Undergraduate Jazz Pedagogy class that I teach, just in the fall, is great because I feel like I’m helping them to understand about teaching and being committed to teaching. And then the rest of the time I have my own band and I have my own freelance work, so it’s very good.
Because if you were full time all the time, something would have to give probably.
Right. Probably. Yeah. But I don’t know, I have good energy, so you never know.
